current_round.prompt:
From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: Bug: goal cancel resolves the active node as default, refusing goals the session actually owns

Body:
Bug: goal cancel resolves the active node as default, refusing goals the session actually owns

  Component: Refine CLI �X goal cancel (active-node resolution / ownership guard)
  Version: refine 4.2.0 (source checkout /insurity/refine @ 7556a231)
  Environment: agent session, REFINE_SESSION_ROLE=agent, daemon refine-8082.service (port 8082); active node bo2lnxnevo03-buddy
  Severity: Medium �X blocks cancelling any goal from an agent session; a fleet transfer workaround exists but is non-obvious and pollutes ownership records.

  Summary

  refine goal cancel <id> reads the active node identity as the literal default node, then rejects the cancel because the goal isn't owned by default. In the same session, at the same moment,
  node list, node activate, goal note, goal retry, goal round, and fleet transfer all resolve the active node correctly as bo2lnxnevo03-buddy. So the ownership-guard resolution path in cancel is
  inconsistent with every other command.

  Steps to reproduce

  1. In an agent session whose active node is bo2lnxnevo03-buddy, own a goal on that node (e.g. fleet transfer bo2lnxnevo03-buddy <goal>).
  2. Confirm active node: refine node list �� active_node_id: bo2lnxnevo03-buddy. refine node activate bo2lnxnevo03-buddy �� active_node_id: bo2lnxnevo03-buddy.
  3. refine goal note <goal> "..." --author Refine �� succeeds (note attaches; proves note resolves active = buddy and the goal is buddy-owned).
  4. refine goal cancel <goal> �� fails:
  Goal <goal> is owned by node bo2lnxnevo03-buddy, not active node default
  5. Loop step 4 five times / re-run immediately after node activate �� identical default result every time (deterministic, not a sync race).

  Expected vs actual

  - Expected: goal cancel uses the same active-node identity as node list/node activate/goal note (bo2lnxnevo03-buddy), sees the goal is owned by the active node, and cancels it.
  - Actual: goal cancel resolves active node as default and refuses. goal note/retry/round on the same goal in the same session succeed, proving the resolution is command-specific.

  Smoking gun

  Back-to-back on the same goal, same session window:
  - goal note <goal> �� success (active resolved = bo2lnxnevo03-buddy, matches owner �� allowed)
  - goal cancel <goal> �� not active node default (active resolved = default, mismatch �� refused)

  Only cancel differs. (Note: goal note also enforces the ownership guard �X before I transferred the goal off bo2lnxnevo02-ethan, note correctly refused with not active node bo2lnxnevo03-buddy �X
  so the guard itself is fine; it's cancel's active-node lookup that returns the wrong value.)

  Workaround used

  refine fleet transfer default <goal> then refine goal cancel <goal> �� succeeds (goal ends cancelled, owned by default). Undesirable: it rewrites ownership to a phantom node just to satisfy the
  mis-resolved guard.

  Suspected root cause (for wherever you fix it in refine proper)

  goal cancel's handler resolves the active node through a different code path than the other goal verbs �X one that falls back to the hardcoded/seed "default" node identity instead of reading the
  machine's activated node id (the value node list/node activate and the note/retry/round handlers use). Likely a missed dependency-injection / wrong-context lookup in the cancel command builder
  specifically.

  Secondary issue (worth fixing alongside)

  The refused cancel prints the error to stdout but exits 0. A guard-rejected cancel should exit non-zero so scripts/agents can detect the refusal instead of parsing the message string.

  Suggested fix

  Make goal cancel resolve the active node via the shared active-node accessor used by goal note/retry/round (single source of truth), add a regression test asserting cancel and note resolve the
  identical active node id in an agent session, and return a non-zero exit on ownership-guard rejection.


[cid:insurity-small2_2f81c33c-d951-4e5c-a467-1113541ca22c.jpg]
Buddy Williams

findings.recommendation: Revise P1 to replace that direct registry lookup with the runtime-root-scoped Node authority, or remove the duplicate prefilter and classify the shared cancellation capability's ownership conflict without losing structured skip reporting.

result.summary: Explicitly route bulk cancellation's ownership prefilter through the port-scoped active-Node authority.
